record.what_it_does: Cloud accounting software for small businesses: invoices, bank feeds, payroll, reporting.
record.auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 authorization code (with PKCE option) is the multi-user method. Xero also has Custom Connections (client credentials) for a single org, which is paid and region-limited. I could not open the OAuth docs page, so this comes from my own knowledge and the MCP README summary.
record.access_notes: The Starter tier is free with a max of 5 connections and no payment method needed. Core (A$35/mo, 50 connections) needs a card. App Certification and a security assessment are listed as prerequisites for the paid tiers. The page's mapping of certification to tiers was unclear. A third-party summary says Starter and Core need no approval, and that certification is mandatory from Plus. A free account can build and test immediately. Public distribution beyond 5 orgs needs a paid tier and likely certification at higher tiers.
record.api_breadth_notes: Separate APIs for Accounting (invoices, contacts, payments, bank transactions, accounts, reports), Payroll (AU/NZ/UK), Assets, Projects, Files, Bank Feeds and Finance. Together these come to well over 50 operations. I did not count them from the docs.
record.mcp_notes: XeroAPI/xero-mcp-server on GitHub, MIT, npm package @xeroapi/xero-mcp-server, run via npx. It is local and supports a bearer token or custom connection client ID and secret. Directories mostly call it official, and one calls it community. I did not verify this on the repo itself.
record.blocker_notes: The free Starter tier caps an app at 5 connected organisations. Real multi-user distribution needs a paid tier (Core from A$35/mo, and higher tiers as scale grows), plus certification and a security assessment for higher tiers. Egress is billed per GB, and reports say daily call caps are 1,000 per org on Starter and 5,000 on Core and above.

evidence.quote: Payment method is not needed for Starter but is required from Core upward.
App Certification is a prerequisite for the paid tiers.

record.needs_human: Several quotes are paraphrased tool summaries of the pricing page, not verbatim page text, and the OAuth, webhooks and OpenAPI pages returned no body. Someone should confirm these on developer.xero.com: the auth methods, webhooks, the OpenAPI spec (the XeroAPI/Xero-OpenAPI repo), the demo company sandbox, and which tiers require certification.
